text: ` What is OOP? A programming approach that organizes software into objects having their own data and behavior. Why do we need OOP?  Large software becomes easy to manage.  Code becomes reusable.  Easy to update.  Easy to understand.  Less chance of bugs. Problem without OOP  One huge program  Everything connected  DiƯicult to modify  More errors  Hard to maintain Solution with OOP  Divide software into objects.  Every object has one responsibility.  Easier maintenance.  Easier debugging.  Better scalability. Real-Life Examples App Used to Learn Swiggy Orders, Menu, Delivery App Used to Learn PhonePe Wallet, Transactions BookMyShow Seats, Booking Razorpay Payments, Refunds Uber Drivers, Trips Zepto Inventory Five Course Modules Module Learn 1 Java Basics 2 Objects & Encapsulation 3 Relationships & UML 4 Inheritance & Polymorphism 5 Design Principles Object Detective Activity For any object ask: Data (Properties)  Name  Color  Size  Price Behavior (Methods)  Start  Stop  Move  Print Lesson Flow Problem → Explanation → Activity → Coding → Quiz → Assignment Key Takeaways  OOP is about organizing software, not just writing code.  Every object has its own responsibility.  OOP makes software scalable, maintainable, reusable, and easier to understand.  The course uses real-world apps to explain concepts.  By the end of the course, you should be able to design software systems, not just write Java programs. Nested if if(){ if(){ } } if inside another if. = vs == = → Assign == → Compare Never write if(flag = true) Write if(flag) or if(flag == true) switch switch(variable){ case value: code; break; default: code; } Use for exact values. break Stops the switch. Without break ↓ Fall Through default Runs when no case matches. Like else. switch vs if Use switch for:  Exact values ("UPI", "MONDAY", 1, 2) Use if/else for:  Ranges (>=, <=, <, >)  Multiple conditions using && or || Ternary condition ? true : false; Shortcut for if-else.

Example String s = age>=18 ? "Adult" : "Minor"; && (AND) Both conditions must be true. Stops at the first false. Example user != null && user.getAge()>18 Protects from NullPointerException. || (OR) Only one condition needs to be true. Stops at the first true. Example hasCoupon || cart>=500 Order of else-if Top ↓ Java checks one by one ↓ First true ↓ Stop Most Common Exam Mistakes  Using = instead of ==  Forgetting break in switch  Writing small ranges before large ones in an else if ladder (e.g., >= 250 before >= 500)  Using switch for ranges like marks > 50  Forgetting that && stops at the first false  Forgetting that || stops at the first true 30-Second Formula Before the Exam  if → one condition  if-else → two choices  else if → many choices (first true wins)  switch → one variable, exact values, use break  default → runs if nothing matches  = → assign, == → compare  ?: → short if-else  && → both true, stops at first false  || → one true is enough, stops at first true For Loop Syntax  for(initialization; condition; update)  {  body;  }  Example  for(int i=0;i<5;i++)  {  System.out.println(i);  }   Order of Execution  Initialization  ↓   Condition  ↓   Body  ↓   Update  ↓   Condition  ↓  

Array Definition Array stores multiple values of the same data type in one variable. Indexes start from 0. Declaration int[] arr = new int[5]; or int[] arr = {10,20,30}; Default Values int → 0 double → 0.0 boolean → false String → null Length arr.length NOT arr.length() Access Element arr[index] Example arr[2] Traverse Array for(int i=0;i<arr.length;i++) { System.out.println(arr[i]); } Reverse Traversal for(int i=arr.length-1;i>=0;i--) { System.out.println(arr[i]); } For-each Loop for(int x:arr) { System.out.println(x); } Use only when index is not required. Sum int sum=0; for(int x:arr) { sum+=x; } Maximum int max=arr[0]; for(int i=1;i<arr.length;i++) { if(arr[i]>max) { max=arr[i]; } } Linear Search for(int i=0;i<arr.length;i++) { if(arr[i]==target) { return i; } } return -1; Common Errors  Wrong i<=arr.length 膆 Correct i<arr.length  Wrong arr.length() 膆 Correct arr.length  Wrong arr[5] (when length is 5) 膆 Last index length - 1  Wrong for(int x:arr) { x=0; } This does not modify the array. Must-Remember Exam Points  Arrays store same data type values.  Array indexing starts at 0.  Last index = length - 1.  arr.length is a field, not a method.  Use for loop when you need the index or want to modify elements.  Use for-each loop when you only need to read values.  ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException
